units.source_text: “我很快就搬进了这户人家，租住了初次来访时，孀妇接待我的那个客厅。

en.t: I soon moved into that household and rented the sitting room where the widow had received me on my first visit.

units.source_text: 这是宅子里最好的一间屋子。

en.t: It was the finest room in the house.

units.source_text: 因为那时，本乡台一带正陆续盖起一些高级寄宿式住宅，所以我清楚地知道，作为一个学生所能住的最好房间是什么样的。

en.t: At that time, superior boarding houses were gradually being built around Hongo-dai, so I knew very well what the best room a student could hope to live in was like.

units.source_text: 我成为新主人的这个房间要比那些寄宿住宅还要漂亮。

en.t: The room of which I had become the new occupant was even finer than those boarding-house rooms.

units.source_text: 刚搬来时，我还觉得自己是个学生，未免太奢侈了些。

en.t: When I first moved in, I even felt that it was somewhat too luxurious for me as a student.

units.source_text: 这是个八叠大的房间，壁龛旁边摆放着一个多宝格架子，对着檐廊有一个壁橱。

en.t: It was an eight-mat room, with a tiered display shelf beside the alcove and a closet facing the veranda.

units.source_text: 虽然一扇窗子也没有，但是朝南的檐廊上总是洒满明媚的阳光。

en.t: Although it did not have a single window, bright sunlight always poured over the south-facing veranda.

units.source_text: 我搬来的那天，看见房间里的壁龛前摆了一瓶插花，插花旁边立着一把古琴。

en.t: On the day I moved in, I saw a vase of arranged flowers placed before the alcove in the room, and beside the flowers stood an old koto.

units.source_text: 花和琴我都看着不顺眼。

en.t: Both the flowers and the koto displeased me.

units.source_text: 我自幼是在嗜好诗书、品茶的父亲身边长大的，从小便受到了唐式风雅情趣的熏陶。

en.t: From childhood I had grown up beside a father who loved poetry, calligraphy, and tea, and from an early age I had been steeped in a refined, Chinese-style taste.

units.source_text: 也许是这个缘故吧，我不知不觉养成了轻视这种庸俗装饰的习性。

en.t: Perhaps because of that, I had unconsciously acquired the habit of looking down on such vulgar decorations.
